bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar panchayat polls only after delimitation: CM Samrat Choudhary – ThePrint – PTIFeed
bihar_raw_news.content: Support our Journalism 9th Anniversary: Free Tote & Mug Subscribe Home India Bihar panchayat polls only after delimitation: CM Samrat Choudhary India Bihar panchayat polls only after delimitation: CM Samrat Choudhary PTI 21 September, 2026 06:48 pm IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ Patna, Sep 21 (PTI) Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Monday said the next panchayat elections in the state will be held only after completion of the delimitation exercise and urged elected representatives of three-tier panchayats to suggest measures for village development. Addressing the ‘Gram Sansad-Bihar Chapter-V, Mukhiya Samvad’ programme here, Choudhary said panchayats are the most important units of grassroots democracy and their elected representatives have a crucial role in addressing public grievances and accelerating development. “The State Election Commission has started the delimitation process, and the next panchayat polls will be held only after its completion. Delimitation of urban local bodies will also be undertaken next year,” the chief minister said. Show Full Article “The prosperity of villages is the prosperity of the country. The country will develop only when villages develop,” he said, urging panchayat representatives to contribute towards the goal of making Bihar a prosperous and empowered state by 2037. He said the government plans to work towards having one panchayat for a population of around 7,500 and an engineering cell would be created in the Panchayati Raj Department to provide technical support for development works. Choudhary also said the government would ensure that at least 30 per cent of products purchased under government schemes are manufactured in Bihar, including steel rods and cement, with the provision being incorporated into the tendering processes. He said Bihar was also working to expand higher education within the state and create employment opportunities for one crore people before 2030 so that people do not have to migrate in search of jobs. The chief minister said farmers were being provided electricity at 55 paise per unit for agricultural use, while all agricultural feeders were being solarised. Each family in Bihar is also being provided 125 units of free electricity per month, he said. PTI PKD MNB This report is auto-generated from PTI news service. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary attends Gram Sansad Bihar Chapter event in Patna
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary attends Gram Sansad Bihar Chapter event in Patna; outlines state growth vision He said, "I believe suggestions should also emerge through the Gram Sansad. We need to discuss how Gram Sansad can advance the vision of a 'Viksit Bharat 2047' envisioned by our respected PM. Former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar envisioned a prosperous Bihar, and the year 2037 will mark a significant milestone for the state. We must also envision how we can make Bihar prosperous during this period.” ANI | Updated: 21-09-2026 15:30 IST | Created: 21-09-2026 15:30 IST Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary (Photo/ANI). Image Credit: ANI Country: India SHARE Key Takeaways AI Summary Analyzing article... Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary emphasised the pivotal role of local governance on Monday, asserting that grassroots leaders hold the true authority in India's administrative framework while outlining a roadmap for a 'Developed Bihar' by 2037, marking 125 years of formation of the state. Addressing the Gram Sansad Bihar Chapter programme in Patna, Choudhary underscored that public policy feedback and governance strategies must originate from village-level institutions to support national growth objectives. He said, "I believe suggestions should also emerge through the Gram Sansad. We need to discuss how Gram Sansad can advance the vision of a 'Viksit Bharat 2047' envisioned by our respected PM. Former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar envisioned a prosperous Bihar, and the year 2037 will mark a significant milestone for the state. We must also envision how we can make Bihar prosperous during this period.” Highlighting the strength of India's three-tier democratic structure, Choudhary challenged conventional notions of political hierarchy, arguing that local village heads carry the heaviest executive responsibilities and wield the most direct influence over community welfare. He said, “Democracy is divided into three tiers. People often say there are three-levels powers in this country: the PM, the CM, and the DM. However, I believe that the most powerful person in this country is the 'Mukhiya' (Village Head), who holds actual authority. They possess the most power and handle the most work.” The Chief Minister also reflected on the intense nature of local politics, noting that contesting elections at the village level presents unique, localised hurdles compared to broader legislative races. “Elections for MLAs or MPs might be easier, but the election to become a 'Mukhiya' becomes increasingly difficult as you go down to the grassroots level," Samrat Choudhary said. On Sunday, CM Samrat Choudhary inaugurated the 'Viksit Bihar: Foundation to Construction' (Viksit Bihar: Neev se Nirman tak) brainstorming session and 'Lav-Kush Pratibha Samman Samaroh' (Talent Felicitation Ceremony) by lighting the ceremonial lamp at the Bapu Sabhagar within the Samrat Ashok Convention Centre. Talented individuals who excelled in various fields were honoured at the event, which was organised by the Progressive Intellectuals Association, Bihar. According to the CMO, the Chief Minister stated that the foundation of unity for the Lav-Kush community was laid in 1994, and this unity remains intact today. bihar_raw_news.title: How Magahi Paan Growers Are Building a Stronger Market Identity | ICAR
bihar_raw_news.content: Collective action, GI authorised-user registration and FPC-based value enhancement are helping Magahi Paan farmers unlock the commercial potential of Bihar’s iconic betel leaf For generations, the farmers of Bihar’s Magadh region have cultivated Magahi Paan, a distinctive variety of betel leaf (Piper betel) valued for its unique flavour, appearance and palatability. Yet, despite its strong traditional identity and commercial importance, farmers had limited awareness of how the product’s Geographical Indication (GI) status could be leveraged to strengthen its market identity and improve value realisation. Magahi Paan received Geographical Indication (GI) registration on 28 March 2018, recognising its distinctive association with Bihar. However, GI registration alone does not automatically translate into greater benefits for individual growers. For farmers to make effective use of the GI identity, awareness about GI provisions, authorised-user registration, branding and collective marketing is crucial. To bridge this gap, the ICAR-All India Co-ordinated Research Project on Medicinal and Aromatic Plants and Betelvine (AICRP-MAP&B), Islampur Centre, Bihar Agricultural University (BAU), Sabour, with technical support from ICAR-Directorate of Medicinal and Aromatic Plants Research, Anand, initiated efforts to sensitise and support Magahi Paan growers in obtaining GI authorised-user registration and strengthening collective value enhancement. Turning a traditional identity into a collective opportunity The GI Registry identifies Bihar as the geographical area for Magahi Paan. The crop is traditionally cultivated across the Magadh region, particularly in Aurangabad, Gaya, Nawada and Nalanda districts. Magahi Paan is recognised by its shiny dark-green, heart-shaped leaves, low pungency and low fibre content, which make the resulting betel quid mild, palatable and easily soluble in the mouth. The presence of eugenol and acetyl eugenol in the leaf oil contributes to its distinctive flavour. While betelvine occupies around 4,000 hectares in Bihar, Magahi Paan is cultivated on approximately 439 hectares, making the strengthening of its identity and value chain particularly important for its growers. Betelvine is a mandate crop of the ICAR-AICRP-MAP&B, coordinated from ICAR-DMAPR, Anand. Through its technical support and farmer-oriented interventions, the programme has been working to connect scientific and institutional support with the needs of growers at the grassroots level. A significant step in this direction came through the efforts of Shri Shiv Shankar Kumar, a progressive Magahi Paan farmer who played a key role in mobilising fellow growers and facilitating the formation of the Renu and Rajendra Magahi Paan Producer Company Limited at Dhevari village, Hisua, Nawada, Bihar. Registered on 11 September 2023 under the Companies Act, 2013, the Farmer Producer Company (FPC) created an institutional platform through which farmers could come together for production, branding, marketing and promotion of Magahi Paan. The collective approach also helped farmers understand that GI recognition could be more than a certification it could become a tool for establishing product identity, strengthening market linkages and creating greater visibility for the growers behind the product. 1,001 farmers take the GI route Through sustained awareness generation, facilitation and coordination, farmers were encouraged to formally associate themselves with the registered GI product. The initiative culminated in the registration of 1,001 Magahi

bihar_raw_news.content: A A A The 2026 Urban Local Body elections were held recently in Rajasthan for 309 urban local bodies and 10,244 wards, with polling held on 09 and 11 September and counting on 14 September. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won 4,182 wards, followed by the Congress with 3,619, while Independents secured 2,273 wards. The results also saw the BJP secure majorities in several municipal corporations, while Congress and Independent candidates won in some others ( here , here ). In this context, a video is circulating on social media ( here , here , and here ), claiming it shows a BJP candidate crying after receiving just one vote in the Rajasthan civic elections. The post also alleges that even his own family members did not vote for him. Let’s verify the claim made in the post in this article. The archived post can be found here . Claim: The video shows a BJP candidate crying after receiving just one vote in the 2026 Rajasthan civic elections. Fact : It is true that a BJP candidate named Kailash Chandra received one vote in the 2026 Rajasthan civic elections. However, the viral video is unrelated to this incident. The man seen in the video is Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Shivchandra Ram, who was seen crying during a press conference in June 2026 after being denied an MLC ticket in Bihar. Hence, the claim made in the post is Misleading . A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to several media reports ( here , here , here , and here ) published in June 2026 featuring the same video. According to these reports, the person seen crying during a press conference is RJD leader and former Bihar minister Shivchandra Ram, who broke down in tears after being denied an MLC ticket. RJD’s Sunil Singh had filed the nomination for the Grand Alliance for one of the 10 seats in the Bihar Legislative Council, which reportedly angered Ram. He alleged that the party had promised to make him an MLC but had betrayed him, following which he announced his resignation from all RJD posts, while clarifying that he had not left the party. This confirms that the viral video is unrelated to the 2026 Rajasthan civic elections. To investigate the claim that a BJP candidate received only one vote in the 2026 Rajasthan civic elections, we conducted a Google keyword search and found multiple reports ( here , here ). According to these reports, BJP candidate Kailash Chandra received only one vote in Ward No. 13 of the Parbatsar Municipality in Rajasthan’s Deedwana-Kuchaman district. Congress candidate Hina Khanam received 376 votes, while Independent candidate Rasheed Khan received 195 votes. The reports also state that Kailash Chandra was a voter in Ward No. 12 but was fielded by the BJP from Ward No. 13, meaning he could not vote for himself. bihar_raw_news.title: Meloni plans to ban burqas and niqabs in Italian schools, cap foreign students in classrooms
bihar_raw_news.content: September 20, 2026 Meloni plans to ban burqas and niqabs in Italian schools, cap foreign students in classrooms Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Associated Press Representational image: women wearing niqabs. Rome, Sep 20 (AP) Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said on Sunday she'll soon introduce a measure to her government that would cap the number of foreign students in classrooms and ban the wearing of burqas and niqabs in schools. Meloni told the youth wing of her nationalist conservative Brothers of Italy party that the measure would also make Italian language lessons compulsory for parents of foreign students having “serious difficulties integrating into the school system.” “For us, anyone who comes to Italy and wants to build their future here must learn our language, understand our culture, and respect our rules,” she said to a standing ovation at the Gioventù Nazionale national festival in Rome. “It is the only serious way to welcome them.” Meloni specifically referred to a ban on the burqa, an all-covering dress worn by some Muslim women, and the niqab, the veil worn by the most conservative Muslim women, in which, at most, only the eyes show. But Meloni didn't mention the hijab, the headscarf worn by some Muslim women. Once approved by the government, the measure would need parliamentary approval within 60 days to pass into law. Meloni, who has political roots in the far-right, has consistently been hawkish on migration. But she has evolved politically over her tenure as prime minister, shifting from a nationalist outlier to an establishment figure among European Union politicians. However, she's also keen to boost her popularity before a general election next year and is introducing a string of policies that achieve that aim, including an exemption from a hated property tax on small- and medium-sized cars and scooters. Earlier this month, Meloni's conservative administration became Italy's longest-serving uninterrupted government since World War II. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar team to study UP's digital sugarcane management system - ChiniMandi
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Top News Trendings AI Representational Image A three-member team from the Bihar government will visit Lucknow on September 21 and 22 to study Uttar Pradesh’s Smart Sugarcane Farmer Portal and e-Ganna app, particularly the state’s digital systems for sugarcane survey, cane supply, payments and grievance redressal, Head Topics reported. The team comprises officials from Bihar’s sugarcane department, the Programme Management Unit (PMU) of the Sugarcane Industries Department and technical agency Dexion India Technology Pvt Ltd. The team will study the digital sugarcane management system at the ground level and understand how various processes are integrated through the Smart Sugarcane Farmer Portal and e-Ganna app. At a meeting to be held at the Lal Bahadur Shastri Sugarcane Farmers Institute, Uttar Pradesh officials will brief the team on online sugarcane surveys, basic quota allocation, sugarcane supply estimates, cane calendars and the transparent issuance of supply slips. The team will also examine the procedures followed for sugarcane supply and payment to farmers. The system that enables farmers to track their cane supplies in real time will be another key area of the study. Online and time-bound grievance redressal mechanisms for sugarcane farmers will also be examined by the Bihar team as part of its assessment of Uttar Pradesh’s digital system. Uttar Pradesh has around 48 lakh sugarcane supplier members. The state’s sugarcane management system is operated through coordination among 158 cooperative sugarcane development societies, 28 sugar mill societies and 121 sugar mills.

Assam, Bengal and Bihar pitch Investors on Eastern Growth Story at ICC Global Business Summit 2026 September 21, 2026 News Category Business EXPORT Global Trade Infrastructure Logistics Organisation Trade NEW DELHI: The inaugural session of the ICC Global Business Summit 2026 , held under the theme “Reinventing Global Business: Growth, Risk & Resilience,” opened at Taj Palace, New Delhi on September 18, bringing together ministers from Assam, West Bengal and Bihar for a session on India’s Eastern and Northeastern growth corridor. Assam Chief Minister Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma opened the ministerial remarks with a data-heavy account of his state’s growth, framing it within what he called the Purvodaya push, the central government’s plan to make the East and Northeast the next engine of national growth. He said Assam’s nominal GSDP is estimated at Rs 7.45 lakh crore for 2025-26, with real growth above 10 percent, projected to rise to Rs 8.71 lakh crore in 2026-27. He cited a Reserve Bank of India report recognising Assam as the fastest growing economy in the country, with industry now accounting for 35.54 percent of the state’s current price GSVA. On execution, Sarma pointed to Assam’s Advantage Assam 2.0 summit, which drew investment commitments of Rs 5.18 lakh crore, of which Rs 3.5 lakh crore has already been converted into on-ground projects within a year. Since May 2021, more than 3,700 new factories have registered in the state, representing close to 1.11 lakh factory jobs, and the single window clearance system has processed over 2.5 million approvals. He highlighted Tata Electronics’ Rs 27,000 crore semiconductor assembly and test facility, expected to be commissioned in December this year with capacity to produce up to 48 million chips a day and generate more than 27,000 direct and indirect jobs, alongside PepsiCo’s recently commissioned food manufacturing facility in the state. On infrastructure, he cited seven operational airports, a new Guwahati terminal designed for roughly 30 million passengers annually, and a multi-modal logistics push spanning the Jogighopa logistics park and the Brahmaputra navigable economic corridor. He also set out plans for 6,000 megawatts of renewable energy capacity by 2030, and cited an export consignment of Assam-grown matcha to Japan. Closing his remarks, Sarma made an unusual offer to investors: round-the-clock access to the state’s top bureaucracy. “A chief minister or a chief secretary, both, or my team, will respond to you even if it is midnight, 2 am, 4 am, anytime, within 5 minutes,” he said. bihar_raw_news.title: Bengal launches 'Seva First' innovation challenge - MillenniumPost
bihar_raw_news.content: Home > Bengal > Bengal launches ‘Seva First’ innovation challenge Bengal Bengal launches ‘Seva First’ innovation challenge BY Dipali Sen 21 Sept 2026 1:31 AM IST X Dipali Sen 21 Sept 2026 1:31 AM IST Kolkata: The West Bengal government on Saturday launched the ‘Seva First Innovation Challenge – Eastern Zone’, inviting students, researchers, start-ups and innovators from West Bengal, Bihar and Jharkhand to identify real challenges in their surroundings and develop practical solutions. The online portal, sficeast.wb.gov.in, was launched at the IIT Kharagpur Research Park in New Town as part of the ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan 2026’. The Department of Science & Technology and Biotechnology (DSTBT) is the nodal department and is organising the initiative in association with six other state departments. The challenge has two categories. School, ITI and polytechnic students and undergraduates can participate in the Junior Category, while graduates, young professionals, researchers, early-stage start-ups, independent innovators and community groups can participate in the Open Category. Participants will be encouraged to identify problems in villages, towns, schools, workplaces and communities, understand whom they affect, develop solutions and demonstrate their impact through implementation. The focus areas include healthcare access, agricultural losses, water shortages, mobility, waste management, education, livelihoods, environmental risks and disaster preparedness. bihar_raw_news.title: Powerful testament to ambition of New India: Nitin Nabin on Delhi-Meerut Expressway
bihar_raw_news.content: Powerful testament to ambition of New India: Nitin Nabin on Delhi-Meerut Expressway IANS September 21, 2026 3:45 PM Share on | New Delhi, Sep 21 (IANS) BJP National President Nitin Nabin on Monday travelled by road from Delhi to Meerut and highlighted the transformation brought by the Delhi-Meerut Expressway, saying the project demonstrated how a long-standing vision could be turned into reality through modern infrastructure. Taking to X, Nabin said, “While travelling from Delhi to Meerut by road today, I experienced firsthand how a vision can truly be turned into reality. A journey that once took over 3 hours can now be covered effortlessly in just 45 minutes.” He said the expressway had become an important part of the daily lives of lakhs of commuters and described the project as an example of the scale and speed of infrastructure development in the country. “The Delhi-Meerut Expressway has become an integral part of the everyday lives of lakhs of commuters. Built under the Bharatmala Pariyojana, it contains India’s first 14-lane expressway section and stands as a powerful testament to the scale, speed and ambition of New India,” Nabin said. Referring to his experience as the Road Construction Department (RCD) Minister of Bihar, the BJP chief said good road connectivity goes beyond simply linking two locations and can have a direct impact on people’s everyday lives. “Having served as the RCD Minister of Bihar, I have seen closely how a good road does more than connect two points on a map. It connects a farmer to a market, a student to a school and a patient to a hospital in time,” Nabin stated. He also linked the development of modern infrastructure with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 25 years of public service, saying such projects show the “kind of India taking shape before us”. “An India where long-held dreams of world-class connectivity are becoming real, and where modern infrastructure is driving us firmly on the fast lane to a Viksit Bharat,” he added. Nabin arrived in Meerut on Monday for a two-day tour of western Uttar Pradesh. This marks Nabin’s first visit to western Uttar Pradesh since assuming the role of National President. Upon his arrival in Meerut on Monday, a large number of BJP workers welcomed him at the Kashi Toll Plaza. Meetings are lined up with former office-bearers, Members of Parliament (MPs), and Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs) from Western Uttar Pradesh. Discussions during these meetings will centre on the state of organisation, preparations for the upcoming elections, and feedback received from the grassroots level. Given the BJP’s recent changes to its organisational structure and the appointment of district in-charges, this visit by the party’s chief is also considered crucial for assessing the activity levels of the new organisational team. --IANS sd/skp

bihar_raw_news.title: Vice-Chancellors of RLBCAU, Jhansi and RPCAU, Pusa, Bihar Visits ICAR-ATARI, Umiam
bihar_raw_news.content: 9 September 2026, Umiam, Meghalaya ICAR-Agricultural Technology Application Research Institute, Zone-VII, Umiam, Meghalaya, had the privilege of welcoming Dr A.K. Singh, Vice-Chancellor, Rani Lakshmi Bai Central Agricultural University (RLBCAU), Jhansi, and Dr P.S. Pandey, Vice-Chancellor, Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University (RPCAU), Pusa, Bihar, on their maiden visit to the institute today. Dr P.S. Pandey, highlighted that extension is not a time-bound activity but a continuous process requiring sustained engagement with farming communities. He stressed that KVKs should therefore be viewed as long-term institutions for technology dissemination, capacity building and livelihood enhancement, rather than merely as short-term project-oriented agencies. He further emphasized that the vision of a truly inclusive and Viksit Bharat cannot be realized without strengthening and supporting KVKs and ensuring their continued engagement with farming communities. Keeping eye upon the complex, risk prone, wide biodiversity of the region, Dr A.K. Singh emphasized the need to assess the performance of KVKs in the North-Eastern region with different parameters as compared to KVKs in plain lands. He stated that the region has small and fragmented landholdings, challenging hilly terrain, limited infrastructure and unique socio-economic conditions, which necessitate a context-specific approach in evaluating agricultural technologies and addressing the emerging and region-specific needs of farmers. Dr A.K. Mohanty, Director, ICAR-ATARI, Umiam gave an overview of the Institute’s new initiatives such as revenue generation, rural agriprenureship, ISO Certification, collaborative research with different ICAR research institutes through Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) across the Northeastern region. The dignitaries interacted with the officials and scientists of ICAR-ATARI, Umiam and exchanged views on strengthening research collaboration, technology application and extension activities, in convergence mode with various agencies to realize the dream of Viksit Bharat @2026. The discussions focused on the strategies to meet the distinctive challenges in the North-Eastern agriculture and the critical role of KVKs in supporting farmers and strengthening the agricultural extension system. The visit of two illustrious Vice Chancellors and the sharing of their rich experiences marked a significant boost to the scientists through their valuable insights into the need for context-specific approaches to agricultural extension, sustained institutional collaboration and stronger coordination among stakeholders for enhancing the impact of KVK in the North-Eastern region. As a lasting footprint of their visit, Dr A.K. Singh, and Dr. P.S. Pandey, planted saplings at the ICAR-ATARI campus, symbolizing their enduring association with the Institute and their shared commitment to the sustainable development of agriculture and the farming community. ICAR-ATARI, Zone-VII, expressed its sincere gratitude to both Vice Chancellors for their gracious visit and valuable interaction. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar infrastructure under lens: Rs 13-crore bridge road cracks in 20 days - The Statesman
bihar_raw_news.content: Barely 20 days after a Rs 13-crore bridge was inaugurated in Bihar’s East Champaran, a roughly 20-foot crack has surfaced on its approach road, and a portion has subsided. In another incident, shuttering at an under-construction flyover collapsed on NH-27 in Muzaffarpur late Sunday. No casualties were reported in the Muzaffarpur incident. The two developments have, however, brought the quality and safety of ongoing infrastructure work under scrutiny. The project was built at a reported cost of around Rs 13 crore. Local residents have reported a crack extending for about 20 feet along the approach road. A portion of the road also appears to have sunk. Residents have questioned the quality of the work and sought a technical enquiry into what caused the damage so soon after the bridge opened. A patch repair has since been carried out on the affected section. Locals, however, have questioned whether it will offer a lasting solution. The bridge was intended to improve connectivity in the area and make access to the district headquarters easier. NH-27 flyover shuttering collapses during concrete casting The second incident occurred at Majhauli Chowk in Muzaffarpur district on Sunday night. Heavy shuttering erected for an under-construction flyover on the Muzaffarpur-Darbhanga section of NH-27 gave way while concrete casting work was underway. The collapse occurred in the Bochahan police station area. The falling structure caused a loud noise and triggered panic at the site. Police and personnel associated with the construction work reached the spot and began removing the fallen material from the road. No casualties were reported. Traffic and pedestrian movement at the site were relatively low because the incident happened late at night. Majhauli Chowk sees substantially greater movement during the day. The flyover construction has also resulted in vehicles using single lanes on either side, according to local reports. The cause of the shuttering collapse has not yet been established. bihar_raw_news.content: Home News National News Crack emerges on newly-built Motihari bridge; flyover shuttering collapses on Muzaffarpur-Darbhanga highway in Bihar In Short A section of shuttering installed for an under-construction flyover on the Muzaffarpur-Darbhanga four-lane highway collapsed at Majhauli Chowk in Muzaffarpur district on Sunday night. IANS Created On: 21 Sept 2026 12:08 PM IST Comment Share : X Crack emerges on newly-built Motihari bridge; flyover shuttering collapses on Muzaffarpur-Darbhanga highway in Bihar A− Font size A+ Select Hans India Now FOLLOW ON G o o g l e News Patna: Two separate infrastructure-related incidents have raised concerns over construction safety and quality in Bihar, with a flyover shuttering collapsing on the Muzaffarpur-Darbhanga four-lane highway and cracks appearing on the approach road of a newly inaugurated bridge in East Champaran. A section of shuttering installed for an under-construction flyover on the Muzaffarpur-Darbhanga four-lane highway collapsed at Majhauli Chowk in Muzaffarpur district on Sunday night. The incident occurred around 10.45 p.m. under the Bochahan police station area while concrete casting work was underway. Heavy-duty shuttering had been installed for the construction of the flyover when a section suddenly gave way during the casting process. The collapse produced a loud noise and triggered panic in the area. Police and personnel from the construction agency reached the spot after receiving information and began clearing the fallen shuttering and debris from the road. No casualties have been reported in the incident. The collapse occurred late at night, when traffic and pedestrian movement at Majhauli Chowk were relatively limited. The location witnesses heavy traffic and pedestrian movement during the daytime, raising concerns about the potential consequences had the structure collapsed during peak traffic hours. The exact cause of the collapse has not yet been established. The construction agency is examining the incident, while questions have also been raised about the safety measures being followed during the ongoing construction work on National Highway-27. Meanwhile, cracks have reportedly appeared on the approach road of the Manjuraha-Hardiya bridge in East Champaran, only around 20 days after its inauguration. The bridge, constructed at a reported cost of approximately Rs 13 crore, is located at Berua Ghat between Manjuraha and Hardiya, near the East Champaran district headquarters. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary inaugurated the approximately 72-metre-long and 7.5-metre-wide RCC bridge on September 1. The project was intended to improve connectivity in the surrounding areas and facilitate easier movement towards the district headquarters. According to local residents, a crack measuring approximately 20 feet has appeared on the approach road. A portion of the road also appears to have subsided, raising concerns about the condition of the newly constructed infrastructure. Locals have questioned the quality of the construction work and demanded a technical enquiry into the cause of the cracking and subsidence. A patch-like repair has been carried out at the affected portion of the approach road. However, residents have questioned whether the repair will provide a permanent solution. Because of the high demand for the aromatic ‘Marcha Chuda’, it is being exported to multiple Indian cities and abroad, increasing demand for cultivation in Champaran's local farmlands. A group of Marcha Chuda cultivators speaking to IANS shared that rising demand for their produce has accelerated cultivation and production. One of the most distinctive features of Marcha Chuda is its unique aroma, which fills their homes and the village with its fragrance. He explained that the GI tag has helped people understand Marcha Chuda’s significance and unique qualities. Ramji Prasad said the specific characteristic derived from Champaran soil distinguishes Marcha Chuda from varieties grown elsewhere. Sharing details of rising income due to increased Marcha Chuda cultivation, he said farmers in certain areas of Champaran are cultivating it and reaping economic benefits. He also urged fellow farmers to increase production, as it helps both farmers and traders capitalise on the rising demand. Marcha Chuda sells for approximately Rs150 per kilogram. Higher demand for the crop means extra income for those involved in its cultivation. Cultivation of Marcha paddy usually begins during the month of Sawan, and the crop is ready for harvest by the end of November. Unlike Marcha Chuda from other regions, Champaran's has a special impact because of its aroma. Farmers cultivate it using traditional, organic methods, without chemicals or fertilisers. The unique shape of Marcha Chuda also sets it apart from other varieties. Its grain resembles a black peppercorn, which is why it is known as 'Marcha' or 'Marcha paddy'. This is currently being transported to states like Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Odisha, Uttarakhand, and Jharkhand. According to Ramji Prasad, his family has been in the Marcha Chuda business since 1969. Initially, this was done entirely by hand-a labour-intensive and time-consuming task - but in 1997, machinery entered the process. national_raw_news.content: India and New Zealand Free Trade Agreement will come into force from 20th of October this year. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said that the Agreement provides duty-free access for 100 per cent of Indian exports to New Zealand. He said, the strategic partnerships reflects the shared ambition to deepen this cooperation and aspirational goal of doubling bilateral trade in goods and services to almost 35 thousand crore rupees in the next 4 to 5 years. This will open new opportunities for Indian exports including textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, engineering goods, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and processed food products. At the same time, New Zealand will gain enhanced and access to the Indian market for products including wood, wool, sheep meat, and raw leather hides. The Agreement also creates new opportunities in services, investment and professional, student and youth mobility, including enhanced pathways for Indian professionals and students. It provides for facilitating 20 billion US dollars of investment into India and strengthens bilateral cooperation in areas including agricultural productivity, pharmaceuticals and medical devices, traditional medicine and AYUSH, technology and trade facilitation. India and New Zealand share longstanding and close relations, anchored in strong people-to-people ties and expanding cooperation across trade and investment, agriculture, education, sports, technology and other areas. The FTA represents a significant step in further strengthening these ties and creating new opportunities for businesses and communities in both countries.

national_raw_news.title: Jan Seva Se Desh Seva: Large number of farmers in MP benefited from PM-KISAN scheme 8 hours ago 141
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service. His journey is guided by the principle of “Jan Seva Se Desh Seva” and a continued commitment to public service. Inspired by this vision of service and good governance, the government is working towards the goal of a developed India by 2047. This commitment, through inclusive development and social empowerment, is bringing about a transformation in people’s lives. In this context, the PM-KISAN scheme has added new achievements to the lives of farmers across the country. In Madhya Pradesh, a large number of farmers are benefiting from the PM-KISAN scheme. Under the scheme, eligible farmers receive financial assistance of Rs 6,000 every year in three equal installments, directly into their bank accounts. This support is useful for farmers to meet their needs for fertilisers, seeds and other farming activities. The scheme was started in 2019. So far, more than Rs 4.47 lakh crore have been transferred to farmers through 23 installments. More than nine crore 49 lakh farmers benefited from the 23rd installment. The Central Government has now approved the continuation of the PM-KISAN scheme from 2026-27 to 2030-31. A total financial provision of Rs 3.15 crore has been made for the scheme. Chhindwara farmer Basant Patel said that farmers are happy with the decision to continue the scheme for five more years. Women farmers have also benefited from the scheme. More than Rs 1.6 lakh crore has been given to women farmers so far. The scheme uses digital verification, Aadhaar authentication and Direct Benefit Transfer to send the money directly to farmers.

national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Finance Appeal to Employees of Public Sector Banks and Regional Rural Banks for Ensuring Uninterrupted Banking Services Posted On: 21 SEP 2026 7:50PM by PIB Delhi The United Forum of Bank Unions and certain other Unions/Associations in the Public Sector Banks (supported by Regional Rural Banks) have called for a series of strikes in support of two principal demands: implementation of five-day banking, and withdrawal of the Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme. Taking due note of the concerns raised, the Government, after detailed discussion, decided to keep the PLI scheme in abeyance. This proactive initiative by the Government fulfilled one of the two main demands of the Unions . Following this, the Government held several rounds of conciliation to address the outstanding issues through dialogue, in keeping with the established practice of resolving differences bilaterally. Despite the Government having resolved one of the two major demands of the union, and sustained conciliatory engagement, a one-day strike was held on 11.09.2026, with a further three-day strike now scheduled from 28.09.2026 to 30.09.2026, and an indefinite strike proposed from 26.10.2026, on the single demand of a five-day workweek for banks. Public Sector Banks play a vital role in the country's economic and social development. They have been at the forefront of financial inclusion, digital banking, financial literacy and rural outreach, ensuring that formal financial services reach every section of society. Recognising this role, and acknowledging that a motivated, secure and efficient workforce is essential for a strong banking system, the Government has taken several measures aimed at improving the working environment, transparency, and welfare of bank employees . Major highlights of these initiatives are as under: Increase in salary and allowances along with fixation of new pay scales for all cadres. Staff Welfare Fund (SWF), a fund allocated by the PSBs for welfare-related activities (health-related expenses, subsidies on canteen, sports and cultural activities, education-related financial assistance, etc.) for working and retired officials of PSBs, was enhanced by 56% in August 2024. The number of executive posts at the levels of Assistant General Manager, Deputy General Manager, General Manager and Chief General Manager were increased. Recruitment of bank employees increased significantly; from FY 2014-15 to FY 2025-26, PSBs recruited ~4,82,800 employees; recruitment doubled in the last three years. As of 01.07.2026, 95.84% of Officers are in position, and 92% of Subordinate/ Award staff are in position. Banking recruitment strengthened with the introduction of Aadhaar authentication and declaration of recruitment results streamlined to reduce attrition in banking recruitment Promotion processes streamlined to ensure timely promotions. Transfer policies improved to enable automated and timely transfers by developing online platforms with the provision to give location preference in case of transfers/promotions. Special leave approved for women employees, including those related to leave during the menstrual period, infertility treatment, adoption of a second child and the events of stillbirth. The President of India will present the prestigious awards, recognising outstanding achievements in Indian cinema for the year 2024. 🎬 लाइट, कैमरा और तैयारियां… गुजरात के एकता नगर, केवड़िया में 72वें राष्ट्रीय फिल्म पुरस्कार समारोह की तैयारियां अब अंतिम चरण में हैं। पर्दे के पीछे की ये झलकियां बता रही हैं कि भारतीय सिनेमा के इस खास जश्न के लिए मंच पूरी तरह तैयार है। ✨ 22 सितंबर को एकता नगर से सजेगा… pic.twitter.com/Ml16gtuZzh — PIB in Gujarat 🇮🇳 (@PIBAhmedabad) September 21, 2026 The National Film Awards are among the most prestigious honours for Indian cinema. Instituted in 1954, the Awards recognise excellence across Feature Films, Non-Feature Films and Writing on Cinema, covering a wide range of languages, regions and forms of filmmaking. Dadasaheb Phalke Award The Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024 will be presented to veteran actor Anant Nag in recognition of his outstanding contribution to Indian cinema. The honour celebrates his remarkable artistic journey and lasting contribution to the rich legacy of Indian cinema. Several other films and artists will also be recognised across different categories, reflecting the diversity and richness of Indian cinema. national_raw_news.content: Media Delegation from Bhopal meets PIB Jammu Director Neha Jalali Home News Details News Details Media Delegation from Bhopal meets PIB Jammu Director Neha Jalali 09/21/2026 J and K JAMMU, Sep 21: A media delegation of ten journalists from Bhopal met Ms. Neha Jalali, Director, PIB Jammu, during its visit to Media Centre Building today. During the interaction, Ms Jalali highlighted the significant developments taking place in Jammu and Kashmir in the areas of connectivity, infrastructure, healthcare, entrepreneurship and economic opportunities following the abrogation of Article 370. She spoke about the expansion and upgradation of road infrastructure across the Union Territory, including the development of major highways, bridges and tunnel networks. Ms Jalali also highlighted developments in the healthcare sector, particularly the establishment and growth of AIIMS Jammu. She noted the institution’s importance in strengthening advanced healthcare facilities in the region and in providing people with greater access to specialised medical services and modern healthcare infrastructure. Speaking about emerging economic opportunities, Ms Jalali highlighted the Aroma Mission and its role in promoting cultivation, value addition and entrepreneurship in the aromatic and allied sectors. She spoke about the potential of such initiatives to provide new livelihood opportunities, encourage local enterprise and support farmers and young entrepreneurs. Ms Jalali further spoke about Jammu and Kashmir’s rich cultural diversity and heritage, highlighting the region’s varied traditions, languages, festivals, handicrafts, arts and cuisines. Later, the delegation, led by Shri Shariq Noor, Deputy Director, Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), Bhopal, visited the Regional Office of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) in Jammu, and undertook a field visit to key highway infrastructure projects in the region. The delegation comprises senior representatives of media organisations based in Bhopal. During the visit, NHAI Project Director Rajiv Kumar briefed the delegation on major highway and tunnel projects being implemented in Jammu and Kashmir. He described National Highway-44 (NH-44) as a key connectivity corridor and informed the delegation that four-laning of the highway is nearing completion, with around 15 km remaining to be four-laned. The delegation was briefed about the Delhi-Katra Expressway and its role in strengthening connectivity between the National Capital Region, Jammu and Katra. Officials also apprised the media representatives about the use of tunnels on the highway corridor, which has reduced the road distance to Srinagar by around 45 km and saves more than an hour of travel time. The earlier road distance was around 300 km. Six tunnels on various highway projects are expected to be completed in the coming year, further strengthening all-weather connectivity in the region. The delegation also visited the Chenani-Nashri Tunnel and was briefed about its construction, operation and role in reducing travel time and improving the reliability of the Jammu-Srinagar highway corridor. The officials further informed the delegation that the Zojila Tunnel is expected to become operational by December 2027. The project is aimed at providing improved and more reliable connectivity between the Kashmir Valley and Ladakh. national_raw_news.title: NSC approves Rs 320 crore plan for Kurukshetra ITI cluster under PM-SETU - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: NSC approves Rs 320 crore plan for Kurukshetra ITI cluster under PM-SETU Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर NSC approves Rs 320 crore plan for Kurukshetra ITI cluster under PM-SETU ANI | Updated: Sep 21, 2026 18:57 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 21 (ANI): The National Steering Committee (NSC) approved a Strategic Investment Plan (SIP) worth Rs 320 crore under PM-SETU for the Kurukshetra ITI Cluster in Haryana, taking the cumulative PM-SETU investment to Rs 2,491 crore across 10 ITI clusters, according to the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). The sanctioned outlay under the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme aims to transform government Industrial Training Institutes into industry-led centres aligned with workforce requirements. Jindal Naveen Avsar Limited partners with the Government of Haryana as the Anchor Industry Partner for the project. The Kurukshetra cluster operates under a Hub-and-Spoke model comprising seven government institutes. Government ITI, Kurukshetra functions as the Hub ITI, while six institutes serve as Spoke ITIs: Government ITI (Women), Kurukshetra; Government ITI, Kaithal; Government ITI (Women), Kaithal; Government ITI, Pehowa; Government ITI, Pabnawa; and Government ITI (Women), Ambala City. Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, said, "Bringing industry closer to ITIs will create stronger employment pathways for our youth. The approval of the Kurukshetra cluster under PM-SETU reflects our commitment to making skill development more relevant, aspirational and responsive to the changing needs of industry." "Through strong industry partnerships, we are working to ensure that young people are equipped with the skills, exposure and opportunities required to participate meaningfully in India's growth story," he added. The Rs 320-crore allocation finances infrastructure strengthening, training facility modernisation, industry-aligned course additions, and trainee employability initiatives. Under the framework, industry partners participate in curriculum design, infrastructure upgrades, training delivery, faculty development, apprenticeships, and placement drives to reflect current market demands. Jindal Naveen Avsar Limited coordinates with the state administration and the member institutes to facilitate apprenticeships, practical instruction, and job placements. The firm also serves as the industry partner for the Barbil ITI Cluster in Odisha, which holds an approved investment plan of Rs 240 crore under the scheme. The broader PM-SETU initiative carries a total outlay of Rs 60,000 crore. The program targets the modernisation of 1,000 government ITIs nationwide through 200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs, alongside capacity augmentation across five National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) to establish sector-specific National Centres of Excellence and expand trainer training systems.
